subject: Technical deep dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs & deployment topology
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Chris Brown <chris.brown@acme.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Technical deep dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs & deployment topology

Hi Chris / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the call today — appreciated the level of detail from your infra and ML teams. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, confirmation of outstanding items, and proposed next steps. Please flag anything we missed.

Summary of pain points and goals
- User-facing recommendation service currently sees p95 latency of ~420ms at median load spikes; target is p95 <= 200ms under normal load and <= 300ms during known traffic bursts.
- Cost per 1M recommendations is higher than expected; looking to reduce inference unit cost by ~30% while preserving model quality.
- Need predictable throughput for peak windows (sustained 1200 rps for 10 minutes; burst to 3500 rps for up to 2 minutes).
- Regulatory constraint: model inputs include PII; must deploy in a VPC with customer-managed KMS and audit logs retained 12 months.

Technical notes from today
- Model: 13B instruction-tuned transformer (HF format). Has a kv-cache friendly architecture; team currently running 4-shard GPUS.
- Sequence length: typical user payload ~512 tokens; tail up to 1024 in diagnostics.
- Current deployment: single-region cloud VPC with autoscaling groups; no service-level rollout strategy for model rollbacks.

Proposed Redwood approach (high level)
- Deployment topology: Dedicated pool in us-west with a private VPC connector to Acme; optional on-prem connector for audit-sensitive flows. See attached proposed-deployment-topology.pdf and network_diagram.png.
- SLOs and capacity: plan to provision baseline capacity to meet sustained 1200 rps with continuous batching, reserve burst capacity for spikes to 3500 rps, and enable preforking + warm KV cache for fast cold-starts.
- Cost optimization: evaluate int8 quantization candidate and batching policy (targeting 25-35% token cost reduction). Redwood Optimize can run a short workload profile to validate quality tradeoffs.

Open questions / action items
1) Can you share sample production traces (latency distribution by payload size) and a representative prompt set? (Chris/Priya)
2) Confirm KMS provider and required key rotation policy. (Acme security)
3) Which regions must remain in-scope for data residency? You mentioned us-west and eu-west previously. (Acme)

Next steps
- Acme to share traces + prompt set by EOD Friday (6/18).
- Redwood to deliver a capacity & cost estimate + deployment diagram by EOD Monday (6/22).
- Technical deep-dive follow-up with Redwood infra team: Wed 6/24 10:00am PT — calendar invite forthcoming.

Attachments: SLO_requirements.xlsx, proposed-deployment-topology.pdf, network_diagram.png

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0127

Subject: Re: Technical deep dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs & deployment topology

Thanks Marissa — this is great and captures the priorities. Quick clarifications:
- We'll export traces and a 48-hour representative prompt sample by Friday EOD (6/18).
- KMS: we use AWS KMS with a 90-day rotation policy and HSM-backed keys for production.
- Regions: primary in us-west; we will need eu-west for EU customers in a later phase (not required for initial pilot).

Question for Redwood: when you say "reserve burst capacity" can you briefly explain how that affects our committed costs vs. burst billing? We're trying to understand trade-offs before the proposal.

I'll loop in our security lead if we need more detail on audit retention.

—Chris

On Tue, 16 Jun 2026 at 15:10, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> 
> Proposed Redwood approach (high level)
> - Deployment topology: Dedicated pool in us-west with a private VPC connector to Acme; optional on-prem connector for audit-sensitive flows.

Hi all — quick note from infra:
- Reserve vs burst: we typically model this as a committed baseline (reserved capacity) sized for sustained load (1200 rps). That shows up as predictable monthly committed units. We then enable burst capacity as billed usage that scales above the reserve. For your use case we can structure a hybrid: a smaller committed pool + burst buffer to reduce committed cost while preserving short bursts.
- Warm KV caching and pre-warmed workers reduce cold-start latency; we'll want to simulate your 2-minute bursts to size the pre-warm policy.
- For quantization/throughput: Ethan will run a short profile on the 13B model (int8 candidate) to estimate CPU/GPU improvements + quality delta.

Ethan, can you confirm ETA for the profiling?

Thanks,
Dylan
Principal Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
